#### 1. nemaline myopathy 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.476)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-390522)

**Proposed mechanism:** DES (HGNC:2918) —DISRUPTS→ intermediate-sized filament organization (GO:0005890); NEB (HGNC:7774) —DISRUPTS→ intermediate-sized filament organization (GO:0005890); intermediate-sized filament organization (GO:0005890) —LEADS_TO→ sarcomere assembly (GO:0043415); sarcomere assembly (GO:0043415) —DISRUPTS→ muscle weakness (HP:0001324); sarcomere assembly (GO:0043415) —DISRUPTS→ hypotonia (HP:0001252); sarcomere assembly (GO:0043415) —DISRUPTS→ exercise intolerance (HP:0009132). Mutations in both DES and NEB disrupt the organization of intermediate-sized filaments, which are crucial for sarcomere assembly. This disruption in sarcomere structure and function leads to the shared phenotypic features of muscle weakness, hypotonia, and exercise intolerance.

**How to falsify it:** If variants in DES and NEB were found to disrupt entirely separate cellular pathways that do not converge on sarcomere assembly or intermediate filament organization, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, if distinct molecular mechanisms (e.g., dominant negative vs. loss of function) were definitively proven for mutations in each gene leading to separate disease pathologies, this would weaken the proposed overlap. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing high frequency (>1%) of pathogenic variants in either DES or NEB.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream effects on sarcomere assembly and intermediate filament organization could reveal common therapeutic targets for both myofibrillar myopathy 1 and nemaline myopathy 2, potentially involving strategies to stabilize sarcomeric structures or improve protein quality control related to these filaments.
